transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, my eating has been really all over the place. Some days I just forget to eat meals, and then other nights I’m up after midnight tearing through takeout and snacks. That’s what kind of scared me into coming in.
During those late-night eating episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating, or does it feel more like you're just eating at a different time than usual?
It feels more like I’m eating at a different time. I’ll barely eat or forget meals during the day, then after midnight I’m going through takeout and snacks.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling persistently low, or a loss of interest or pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?

Yeah… I haven’t really wanted to do much of anything lately. I used to play soccer on weekends, cook for my girlfriend, go check out little galleries, even help the newer sales guys out. Now I just can’t seem to care enough to do any of it.
Has this low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day for the past two weeks or longer?
Yeah. It’s been going on for about four months, really—the low mood, feeling guilty, not caring about stuff. It got harder to ignore after the trouble at work.
Did this pattern of skipping daytime meals and eating heavily after midnight start before your mood changes four months ago, or did it begin around the same time?

Honestly, I’m not sure exactly when it started. But my eating’s been really all over the place—some days I completely forget meals, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. That’s what really scared me enough to come in.
Do you find yourself waking up in the middle of the night and feeling like you need to eat something in order to fall back asleep?
Yeah, sometimes I wake up and end up eating a bunch of takeout or snacks after midnight. Other days, though, I’ll just forget to eat altogether. It’s been really up and down.
In the mornings, do you typically have little to no appetite—like you're just not hungry—rather than simply not having time or motivation to eat?

Honestly, it’s just really inconsistent. Some days I forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. That’s the part that scared me enough to come in.
Would you say this pattern of skipping meals during the day and eating heavily after midnight has been happening on most days for at least the past three months?

I’m not sure if it’s been most days for three months exactly. I just know it’s been really erratic—skipping meals some days, then eating a lot of takeout and snacks late at night. That’s what worried me.
Besides the low mood and loss of interest, have you noticed trouble concentrating, low energy, or feelings of worthlessness nearly every day during this time?
Yeah. I keep replaying every mistake I made with those Providence accounts. It feels like I blew my whole future, like I’m useless and everyone at work can see it.
Over the past few months, have you noticed any significant change in your weight—either gaining or losing—since this eating pattern started?
I’m not sure about my weight exactly. What’s really changed is how all over the place my eating is—some days I forget meals, then other nights I’m eating a ton of takeout and snacks after midnight.
On days when your mood feels a bit better or less heavy, do you still notice this same pattern of skipping meals during the day and eating heavily after midnight?
Honestly, even when I feel a little less weighed down, my eating is still all over the place. I’ll forget meals during the day, then end up going through takeout and snacks after midnight.
Do you find that you can't fall back asleep at night unless you eat something, as if the eating itself is what allows you to get back to sleep?
I don’t know if it’s that I can’t sleep unless I eat. Sometimes I’m just awake and end up eating, but I haven’t really noticed the food being what gets me back to sleep.
When something good happens—like a compliment or good news—does your mood actually brighten for a while, even briefly, or does it stay low no matter what happens?
I’m not really sure. I guess good things can feel nice for a minute, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it actually changes my mood for long.
Thinking back further, did you notice this pattern of skipping daytime meals and eating heavily after midnight at any point before the past four months, even when your mood was normal?

Honestly, I can’t really say for sure before the last few months. What I do know is lately it’s been really all over the place—forgetting meals some days, then eating a ton of takeout and snacks after midnight.

Aside from how it relates to your mood, does this pattern of skipping meals and eating heavily at night bother you or cause problems in your life on its own—like guilt about the eating itself, or trouble functioning because of it?

Yeah, it does bother me. It’s honestly what scared me enough to come in—the way I’ll forget meals completely some days, then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. It just feels really all over the place.

Before the last four months—say, six months to a year ago—were you already skipping meals during the day and eating most of your food late at night, even when your mood and interest in things were completely normal?

I’m not sure about that far back. What I know is that lately my eating’s been really all over the place—some days I’ll forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m eating a lot of takeout and snacks after midnight.
Was there ever a period, even briefly, in the last four months when your mood and interest in things improved but the skipping-meals-and-eating-after-midnight pattern completely went away?
I don’t know if it completely went away. The eating’s been all over the place—some days I forget meals, and then other nights I’m eating a lot of takeout and snacks after midnight.
Over the past month, on how many nights per week would you say you wake up and eat after midnight?
I’m not sure how many nights exactly. It happens some nights—I’ll be up after midnight eating takeout and snacks—but I haven’t really counted it per week.
Would you say that most of your daily food intake happens after dinner and after midnight, rather than earlier in the day?

Honestly, a lot of it does end up being late. Some days I barely eat or forget meals, then I’m eating takeout and snacks after midnight. It’s been pretty all over the place, and that’s what worried me.
In the mornings, do you actually feel physically not hungry—like food seems unappealing or you have no appetite—or do you just not feel motivated or energetic enough to eat?
It’s hard to say. Some days I just forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. It’s been really all over the place.
